p01-neuron-title.name: p01-neuron-title
p01-neuron-title.text: The "neuron" for prediction: weight, add a bias, then a hard limiter decides the class

p01-neuron-ctx.name: p01-neuron-ctx
p01-neuron-ctx.text: Draw the perceptron's prediction as a flow. Take data point 1: $\mathbf x=(1.8,1.8)$, $\mathbf w=(0.3,-0.4)$, $b=0.2$ (this page only predicts, no training).

p01-neuron-src.name: p01-neuron-src
p01-neuron-src.text: Source: KP05 lecture §1.1 (weighted sum and hard limiter); the diagram is an editable computation flow, not an exact model of a biological neuron.

p01-neuron-c0.name: p01-neuron-c0
p01-neuron-c0.text: Left to right: how does the input become $\pm1$? First find where the "weighted sum" is.

p01-neuron-c1.name: p01-neuron-c1
p01-neuron-c1.text: Multiply then add: $0.3(1.8)+(-0.4)(1.8)=-0.18$. Weighted sum $\sum w_jx_j=-0.18$.

p01-neuron-c2.name: p01-neuron-c2
p01-neuron-c2.text: Then add the bias: $z=-0.18+0.2=0.02$. If the threshold is written $\theta$, then $b=-\theta$.

p01-neuron-c3.name: p01-neuron-c3
p01-neuron-c3.text: $h(z)=\begin{cases}+1,&z\ge0\\-1,&z<0\end{cases}$. $z=0.02\ge0$, so the prediction is $\widehat y=+1$ (positive); point 1's true label is also $+1$.

p01-neuron-c4.name: p01-neuron-c4
p01-neuron-c4.text: The neuron only describes "how to predict": it outputs a discrete class, not a probability, and does not guarantee correct answers on new data. "How to train" is a separate matter (next page).

p02-tie-title.name: p02-tie-title
p02-tie-title.text: What about zero? Prediction assigns it to the positive class, but training counts it as "needs correction"

p02-tie-ctx.name: p02-tie-ctx
p02-tie-ctx.text: Prediction ($z\ge0\Rightarrow+1$) and the training condition for correction ($m=y\,z\le0$) treat $z=0$ differently; both exist to settle ties explicitly.

p02-tie-src.name: p02-tie-src
p02-tie-src.text: Source: KP05 lecture §1.1: prediction favors the positive class; "training still counts every zero score as needing correction, stricter than the prediction tie rule".

p02-tie-c0.name: p02-tie-c0
p02-tie-c0.text: When z is exactly 0, which class is the point predicted as? Is it counted as correct or as needing correction?

p02-tie-c1.name: p02-tie-c1
p02-tie-c1.text: Prediction: $z\ge0\Rightarrow\widehat y=+1$. A zero score goes to the positive class (this lecture's choice).

p02-tie-c2.name: p02-tie-c2
p02-tie-c2.text: Training: only $m\le0$ needs correction, so $m=0$ is corrected too (the red zone includes 0).

p02-tie-c3.name: p02-tie-c3
p02-tie-c3.text: So for the same point at $z=0$: prediction says "positive", training says "still needs correction". Training is stricter: a tie rule cannot make it count as correct.

p03-eleven-title.name: p03-eleven-title
p03-eleven-title.text: Eleven points: how many does the current boundary get right? Which ones are wrong?

p03-eleven-ctx.name: p03-eleven-ctx
p03-eleven-ctx.text: The first 5 points are positive (blue circles), the last 6 negative (red triangles). Start $\mathbf v_0=(0.3,-0.4,0.2)$, learning rate $\rho=0.35$.

p03-eleven-src.name: p03-eleven-src
p03-eleven-src.text: Source: KP05 lecture §1.3 eleven points (data of the source's interactive program, not claimed to be the textbook figure's complete raw data); this data cannot be split by a line, exactly the case the pocket method handles.

p03-eleven-c0.name: p03-eleven-c0
p03-eleven-c0.text: See whether blue circles and red triangles are mixed: can one line separate them completely?

p03-eleven-c1.name: p03-eleven-c1
p03-eleven-c1.text: Green line $0.3x_1-0.4x_2+0.2=0$: points with positive $m=y\,g$ are correct. Correct count $C(\mathbf v_0)=8$.

p03-eleven-c2.name: p03-eleven-c2
p03-eleven-c2.text: The red circles are the three points with $m\le0$: points 8, 9, 10 (all negative). Their $m$ are $-1.34,-1.25,-0.44$ in turn.

p03-eleven-c3.name: p03-eleven-c3
p03-eleven-c3.text: However the boundary is placed, blue circles and red triangles are mixed: the data is not linearly separable, so $Y$ can never become empty.

p03-eleven-c4.name: p03-eleven-c4
p03-eleven-c4.text: The earlier stopping condition ($Y=\emptyset$) cannot be reached. We need an approach that does not rely on it: just ask "how many are right at best so far". Starting score: $8$.

p04-worse-title.name: p04-worse-title
p04-worse-title.text: Run one batch update: the wrong points are "corrected", yet overall 8 correct become 4 correct

p04-worse-ctx.name: p04-worse-ctx
p04-worse-ctx.text: The update rule is the same as KP02: $\mathbf v_1=\mathbf v_0+\rho\sum_{i\in Y}y_i\mathbf a_i$ (the lecture writes it with $\delta=-y$ as $\mathbf v_0-\rho\sum\delta\mathbf a$).

p04-worse-src.name: p04-worse-src
p04-worse-src.text: Source: KP05 lecture §1.3: $\sum\delta_i\mathbf a_i=(3.1,-3.75,3)$, $\mathbf v_1=(-0.785,0.9125,-0.85)$; rescoring the 11 points gets only 4 correct; numbers recomputed by build_kp05_en.py.

p04-worse-c0.name: p04-worse-c0
p04-worse-c0.text: Predict: after summing the requests of the three wrong points 8, 9, 10 and updating, will the number of correct points rise or fall?

p04-worse-c2.name: p04-worse-c2
p04-worse-c2.text: The orange line is the boundary after the update. Rescoring the 11 points: only $4$ correct, fewer than the start's $8$.

p04-worse-c4.name: p04-worse-c4
p04-worse-c4.text: Compare $c=4<H=8$: do not replace; the pocket keeps the starting weights. That is the point of "historical best".

p05-curve-title.name: p05-curve-title
p05-curve-title.text: Repeat 80 times: the current error count wobbles, the pocket's error count never gets worse

p05-curve-ctx.name: p05-curve-ctx
p05-curve-ctx.text: Same 11 points, same start and $\rho=0.35$, run batch updates in a row. After each update record: the error count of the current weights and of the pocket (historical best).

p05-curve-src.name: p05-curve-src
p05-curve-src.text: Source: This curve is recomputed by build_kp05_en.py for 80 updates of the lecture's algorithm (the same flow as the lecture's [supplement] code), not a new experiment; batch updates are deterministic, with no randomness.

p05-curve-c0.name: p05-curve-c0
p05-curve-c0.text: After each update, how does the current weights' error count change? And the pocket's? Guess first.

p05-curve-c1.name: p05-curve-c1
p05-curve-c1.text: Blue line = current error count: start $3$, one update gives $7$, then it wobbles between $3\sim8$ without settling.

p05-curve-c2.name: p05-curve-c2
p05-curve-c2.text: Green line = pocket error count: it falls only when something better appears, so it never rises. In these 80 updates nothing beats the start (the minimum is only $3$), so the pocket stays the start, the green line is flat and ends at $3$.

p05-curve-c3.name: p05-curve-c3
p05-curve-c3.text: Pocket rule: store the start first, $H\leftarrow C(\mathbf v_0)$; afterwards only a candidate with $c>H$ replaces both $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{best}}$ and $H$, and ties keep the old one. So $H_{t+1}\ge H_t$.

p06-limits-title.name: p06-limits-title
p06-limits-title.text: What does the pocket guarantee, and not guarantee? What to watch for in implementation?

p06-limits-ctx.name: p06-limits-ctx
p06-limits-ctx.text: The pocket only guarantees "the historical best never gets worse". The three things below must not be confused with it.

p06-limits-src.name: p06-limits-src
p06-limits-src.text: Source: KP05 lecture §1.4 and [verification limit]: only the abstract of Gallant (1990) was read, and the assumptions of the full optimality theorem were not verified, so neither this lecture nor this deck applies asymptotic optimality of the randomized version.

p06-limits-ca0.name: p06-limits-ca0
p06-limits-ca0.text: Guaranteed: the pocket's correct count does not decrease.

p06-limits-cb0.name: p06-limits-cb0
p06-limits-cb0.text: Follows directly from "replace only if c>H".

p06-limits-ca1.name: p06-limits-ca1
p06-limits-ca1.text: Not guaranteed: it is not necessarily the best of all lines.

p06-limits-cb1.name: p06-limits-cb1
p06-limits-cb1.text: Lecture [verification limit]: global optimality not verified.

p06-limits-ca2.name: p06-limits-ca2
p06-limits-ca2.text: Not guaranteed: best on the training set does not mean best on new data.

p06-limits-c0.name: p06-limits-c0
p06-limits-c0.text: What does each of these three say? First decide which one is guaranteed.

p06-limits-c1.name: p06-limits-c1
p06-limits-c1.text: The wrong way: `best = v` just makes two names point to the same array, so when `v` changes later, the pocket changes too.

p06-limits-c2.name: p06-limits-c2
p06-limits-c2.text: Correct: `best = v.copy()`, the pocket is an independent copy.

p07-practice-title.name: p07-practice-title
p07-practice-title.text: Practice: find the new weights, and decide whether we can decide to swap the pocket

p07-practice-ctx.name: p07-practice-ctx
p07-practice-ctx.text: Work it out first. Hint: the update is $\mathbf v_{\text{new}}=\mathbf v-\rho\sum\delta\mathbf a$ (the lecture's $\delta$ convention). After the update what else is missing to compare? Press Next when done.

p07-practice-src.name: p07-practice-src
p07-practice-src.text: Source: KP05 lecture practice; answer computed by build_kp05_en.py (v=(0.8, 0.6, −0.6)) and recomputed independently by check_numbers_kp05.py.

p07-practice-q.name: p07-practice-q
p07-practice-q.text: Given: $\sum\delta\mathbf a=(2,-1,4)^T$, $\mathbf v=(1,0.5,-0.2)^T$, $\rho=0.1$. (a) The new $\mathbf v$? (b) From these numbers alone, can we decide whether to replace the pocket?

p07-practice-a2.name: p07-practice-a2
p07-practice-a2.text: (b) No. Replacement compares $c>H$: the candidate's correct count $c=C(\mathbf v_{\text{new}})$ against the pocket's current $H$. Here we have only weights and a correction, no data and no $H$, so $c$ cannot be computed.

p07-practice-a3.name: p07-practice-a3
p07-practice-a3.text: To decide we also need: rescore all the data to get $c$, and the $H$ stored in the pocket; swap only if $c>H$.

p08-summary-title.name: p08-summary-title
p08-summary-title.text: Summary: the neuron predicts, training keeps the best in the pocket

p08-summary-ctx.name: p08-summary-ctx
p08-summary-ctx.text: Recall along the 11-point example; the five conclusions of this KP are on the right.

p08-summary-e0.name: p08-summary-e0
p08-summary-e0.text: Neuron = weighted sum + bias + hard limiter; prediction $z\ge0\Rightarrow+1$, but training counts every $m\le0$ (including 0) as needing correction

p08-summary-e1.name: p08-summary-e1
p08-summary-e1.text: When not separable $Y$ never becomes empty; one update can get worse (8 correct → 4 correct)

p08-summary-e2.name: p08-summary-e2
p08-summary-e2.text: Pocket: store the start and compute $H$; only $c>H$ replaces both $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{best}}$ and $H$; $H$ never decreases

p08-summary-e3.name: p08-summary-e3
p08-summary-e3.text: The guarantee is only the historical best; not the global best, not the test best; set an update budget and return an independent copy

p08-summary-e4.name: p08-summary-e4
p08-summary-e4.text: Open question: with 3 or more classes, how do we write "the highest score wins" as a learnable constraint? Next KP: the Kesler construction
